newsitem.title: UK: NatWest weakens as results fail to sparkle.
newsitem.headline: NatWest weakens as results fail to sparkle.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc edged lower at the start of trading on Tuesday after the banking group's first-half profits provided few positive surprises, dealers said.
The stock was down 10p at 860 by 0730 GMT in volume of 306,267 shares, after on Monday closing near its record high of 897p set on July 4.
In stark contrast with sharp share price gains after recent results from HSBC Holdings and Lloyds TSB Plc, NatWest shares showed no sign of shaking off their discount rating to leading rivals.
"There is nothing in the figures to suggest any further black holes...but I can't see anything sparkling in there," said a dealer at one top investment bank.

"The bad news is in the price but if you are a seller you are probably still a seller and if you are a buyer you are probably still a buyer...I can't think anyone is going to change their views on the basis of these results."

Dogged in recent months by losses in derivatives trading at its NatWest Markets unit, NatWest shares have underperformed other banks which have focused more on expanding their domestic retail operations where profits have soared.
Yet dealers noted that NatWest had already detailed a reorganisation of its investment banking operations and that perhaps the bad news had been discounted.
"The initial reaction will probably be to call them lower," said one senior dealer, "but the comment from analysts will probably be to the effect that we have seen the worst."
NatWest said pre-tax profit on continuing operations, excluding a charge of 106 million stg, rose 17 percent to 775 million stg from 662 million a year before.
Analyst forecasts had been mostly in a range between 757 million stg and 770 million.
The interim dividend was raised 10.4 percent to 10.6p, matching forecasts.

In line with its previous statements, NatWest said its treasury business would become a separate sector while its NatWest Markets unit would be "taken forward under new leadership on a clearly focused basis with close regard to profitability."
In retail and commercial banking, NatWest said it was imperative that it cut costs significantly and made better use of existing customer relationships.
By 0741 GMT the stock had recovered to be down just 3p at 867.
HSBC also bounced from an initial decline to be up 6p at 22.44 stg, while Lloyds was up 10-1/2p at 740-1/2.
